audit.why: Ranged laner who wins the walk-up phase; Aatrox needs to reach him. Existing chart favouring Akshan early and Aatrox once he can close is consistent with the kit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 phase text was a generic template that named no ultimate and no cooldown.
audit.why: Comeuppance (R) is 100/85/70 and channels stored bullets from range. World Ender reveals stealth, which is the direct counter to Going Rogue (W, 18/14/10/6/2).
audit.corrected: Comeuppance (R) charges bullets from range on 100s, but World Ender reveals stealth — ult when he vanishes into Going Rogue (W) and he cannot reposition out of your Q pattern.

audit.whatIsWrong: Key Ability Interactions described Infernal Chains (W) as a root; Riot’s text says enemies are dragged back to the centre if they do not leave the zone, and the decisive interaction for this matchup was absent.
audit.why: World Ender (R) reveals stealth — that is the answer to Akshan's whole vanish-and-reposition pattern. Heroic Swing (E, 18/16.5/15/13.5/12) needs terrain, so fighting him away from walls removes his escape.
audit.corrected: Your Q sweetspot (outer edge) is your damage and your heal — land the edge, never the inner hit, and use E mid-cast to swing the sweetspot onto Akshan. Infernal Chains (W) drags him back to the centre if he doesn't leave the zone — hold it for Heroic Swing (E, 18s at rank 1), which needs terrain, so fight him off the wall and he has no exit. Vs a ranged laner save E to close, not for chip. World Ender reveals stealth: pop it when he goes invisible in Going Rogue (W) and the vanish stops working.

W (Infernal Chains) roots him if he doesn't leave the zone: use it to lock him for Q2/Q3 or to cut off his escape. Vs a ranged laner, save E to close the gap or dodge poke — not for chip damage; you only win once you're on top of him. Pop R (World Ender) for the heal, AD and move speed when you fully commit or to survive his ultimate — never burn it for a single Q.
